title: Rectification and localization properties of the projective chain model
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Equip the unbounded cochain complexes $\operatorname{Ch}(R)$ with the projective closed symmetric monoidal model structure of [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model], using the cochain and quasi-isomorphism conventions of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Thus weak equivalences are quasi-isomorphisms, fibrations are degreewise surjections, tensor is the direct-sum total tensor with Koszul signs, and its unit is $R[0]$. This model structure is left proper (pushouts of weak equivalences along cofibrations are weak equivalences) and tractable (locally presentable, with the two lifting systems generated by sets and generating cofibrations between cofibrant objects). It satisfies the monoid axiom: pushouts and transfinite composites of maps $j\otimes C$, where $j$ is a trivial cofibration and $C$ is any complex, are weak equivalences; trivial means also a weak equivalence. Every complex is fibrant and $R[0]$ is cofibrant. For a cofibrant complex $P$ and any $C$, morphisms $P\to C$ in the localized homotopy category are chain maps modulo chain homotopy; a homotopy from $f$ to $g$ is a degree-$(-1)$ map $h$ with $f-g=dh+hd$.

The homotopy coherent monoidal localization of this model, with the convention of [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability], is the presentably symmetric monoidal derived infinity-category $\mathbf D_\infty(R)$. Its tensor is computed on cofibrant replacements and preserves small colimits separately. A chain map becomes an equivalence in this localization if and only if it is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Example 5.11, unbounded complexes, and Theorem 5.8 hypotheses. For localization homotopy classes and saturation: Hovey, Model Categories, Theorem 1.2.10(ii),(iv); for projective fibrations and chain homotopy: Hovey, Model Categories, Theorem 2.3.11 and the following paragraph; for monoidality: Proposition 4.2.13. Haugseng read online; Hovey text inherited in the sandbox, neither archived in literature/. No Stacks tag supplies this model structure.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] over the given commutative ring $R$. It supplies the unbounded combinatorial closed symmetric monoidal model, its generating sets, its degreewise split cofibrations with dg-projective cokernel, and its cofibrant unit $R[0]$. In particular $C\to0$ is degreewise surjective for every complex $C$, so every object is fibrant. Keep its total tensor and total Hom conventions throughout.

source.place: Theorem 2.3.11 and Proposition 4.2.13, cochain reindexing; all-fibrant assertion immediately after Theorem 2.3.11.

proof.text: For every integer $n$, the sphere $S^n$ of Step 1 is dg-projective: its terms are free or zero and $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(S^n,N)$ is the reindexed complex $N$ with the shift sign, hence is acyclic when $N$ is acyclic. Thus $0\to S^n$ is a cofibration by the cokernel criterion in [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model]. Since $S^{n+1}\to D^n$ is a generating cofibration, composition with $0\to S^{n+1}$ makes $D^n$ cofibrant too; composition preserves the left lifting property by composing two diagonal fillers. The sources and targets of both generating sets $S^{n+1}\to D^n$ and $0\to D^n$ are therefore cofibrant. Local presentability and generation of both lifting systems by sets already come from Step 1. These assertions give tractability, also with the convention requiring both generating sets to have cofibrant sources.

source.place: Definition 2.3.3 and Theorem 2.3.11; cofibrant generating objects checked directly.

proof.text:
For left properness, let $i:A\to B$ be a cofibration and $f:A\to A'$ a quasi-isomorphism. Put $B'=B\amalg_AA'$, let $g:B\to B'$ be the induced map, and put $T=B/A$. The degreewise splitting in [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] identifies the pushout degree by degree with $A'\oplus T$, so $0\to A'\to B'\to T\to0$ is exact and the map on quotients is $1_T$. Using the cone differential of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the two inclusions $A\to B$ and $A'\to B'$ give a degreewise short exact sequence
$$0\to\operatorname{Cone}(f)\to\operatorname{Cone}(g)\to\operatorname{Cone}(1_T)\to0.$$
Writing $i':A'\to B'$ for the pushout inclusion and $p:B\to T$, $p':B'\to T$ for the quotient maps, the cone inclusion is $(a',a)\mapsto(i'a',ia)$ and the cone quotient is $(b',b)\mapsto(p'b',pb)$. The equality $gi=i'f$ makes these chain maps; degreewise split exactness of the two rows makes their kernel and image agree. Its degree-$n$ quotient is $T^n\oplus T^{n+1}$ and its differential is $(x,y)\mapsto(d_Tx+y,-d_Ty)$.

source.place: Agent cone calculation of the pushout of a degreewise split monomorphism; cone convention from the cited definition.

proof.text: By [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic], $\operatorname{Cone}(f)$ is acyclic. The degree-$(-1)$ map $(x,y)\mapsto(0,x)$ contracts $\operatorname{Cone}(1_T)$: applying its differential before and after this map gives sum $(x,y)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] to the short exact sequence of Step 3. The segment $H^n\operatorname{Cone}(f)\to H^n\operatorname{Cone}(g)\to H^n\operatorname{Cone}(1_T)$ has zero outside terms, so the middle term is zero in every degree. The cone criterion now makes $g$ a quasi-isomorphism. This proves left properness for arbitrary $A,A'$, without a cofibrancy assumption on them.

source.place: Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic, and its cone-triangle interpretation; homology.tex Tag 0117, lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain. Agent application to Step 3.

proof.text: Let $j:A\to B$ be a trivial cofibration and $Q=B/A$. By [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model], $j$ is degreewise split and $Q$ is dg-projective. In the long exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact], both $H^n(A)\to H^n(B)$ and $H^{n+1}(A)\to H^{n+1}(B)$ are isomorphisms, forcing $H^n(Q)=0$. Thus $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q,Q)$ is acyclic by dg-projectivity. Its degree-zero cycle $1_Q$ is a boundary, giving a degree-$(-1)$ map $s:Q\to Q$ with $d_Qs+sd_Q=1_Q$. Here the Hom differential on a degree-$r$ map $u$ is $D(u)=d u-(-1)^r u d$.

source.place: Paragraph after Theorem 2.3.11: trivial cofibrations have projective complex cokernels; direct contraction argument from the cited dg-projective criterion.

proof.text: Choose a graded section $t:Q\to B$ of $B\to Q$. Its defect $d_Bt-td_Q$ factors uniquely as $j a$, with $a:Q\to A$ of degree $1$, and squaring the differential gives $d_Aa+ad_Q=0$. With $s$ from Step 5, set $u=t+j a s$. Since $D(a s)=-a(d_Qs+sd_Q)=-a$, we obtain $D(u)=0$, and the projection of $u$ to $Q$ remains $1_Q$. Consequently $(j,u):A\oplus Q\to B$ is an isomorphism of complexes identifying $j$ with the first summand inclusion.

source.place: Agent explicit splitting calculation for the projective cokernel described after Theorem 2.3.11; the sign in the correction is plus.

proof.text: For any complex $C$, the isomorphism of Step 6 identifies $j\otimes C$ with $A\otimes C\to(A\otimes C)\oplus(Q\otimes C)$. The map $S(q\otimes c)=s(q)\otimes c$ contracts $Q\otimes C$: for homogeneous $q$ of degree $a$, the two terms involving $s(q)\otimes d_Cc$ have signs $(-1)^{a-1}$ and $(-1)^a$, so they cancel, and $dS+Sd=(d_Qs+sd_Q)\otimes1=1$. A pushout along any map $A\otimes C\to V$ is therefore $V\to V\oplus(Q\otimes C)$, a chain homotopy equivalence. For the inclusion $k:V\to V\oplus(Q\otimes C)$, its projection $r$ satisfies $rk=1_V$. On the direct sum, the degree-$(-1)$ map $H(v,w)=(0,S(w))$ satisfies $dH+Hd=1-kr$, proving the other inverse identity up to chain homotopy. On cohomology a homotopy contributes only boundaries, so this pushout is a quasi-isomorphism. No flatness assumption on $C$ is needed. Coproducts of such maps have the same description, using $\bigoplus_\lambda H_\lambda$; every element has finite support, so this degree-$(-1)$ map is defined and satisfies the contraction identity componentwise.

source.place: Example 5.11, monoid-axiom hypothesis of Theorem 5.8; agent tensor-sign and pushout calculations supplying the argument.

proof.text:
Consider a small ordinal-indexed continuous sequence $(V_\alpha)$ whose successor maps are pushouts as in Step 7. Prove by transfinite induction that $V_0\to V_\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism. At $0$ it is the identity; at successors use Step 7 and composition of cohomology isomorphisms. At a nonzero limit ordinal $\beta$, its predecessors are a nonempty directed set and $V_\beta=\varinjlim_{\alpha<\beta}V_\alpha$ degreewise. Exact filtered colimits of modules, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian], give
$$H^n(V_\beta)\cong\varinjlim_{\alpha<\beta}H^n(V_\alpha).$$
For this equality, apply exactness to the sequences $0\to Z^nV_\alpha\to V_\alpha^n\to\operatorname{im}d_\alpha^n\to0$ and $0\to\operatorname{im}d_\alpha^{n-1}\to Z^nV_\alpha\to H^nV_\alpha\to0$ and to the inclusions of the images in the adjacent terms: kernels, images and the indicated quotients are thereby identified with those after the colimit. The induction maps from $H^n(V_0)$ identify this diagram with a constant diagram of isomorphisms, whose colimit is $H^n(V_0)$. This proves the limit step and hence the monoid axiom. A zero-length composite is included as the identity.

source.place: Tag 00DB, lemma-directed-colimit-exact. Agent transfinite induction applied to Step 7; consistent with Haugseng Example 5.11.

proof.text: If $P$ is cofibrant, [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model] says that $P$ is dg-projective. For an acyclic $N$, any chain map $P\to N$ is a degree-zero cycle in the acyclic complex $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,N)$, hence is $d_Nh+hd_P$ for a degree-$(-1)$ map $h$. Thus $P$ is K-projective in the null-homotopy convention of [lem-coef-kprojective-derived-hom-bijection]. Apply that bijection with $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, which is abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian], to any complex $C$. Its domain is exactly chain maps modulo the homotopies $f-g=d_Ch+hd_P$. The projective model has a zero object, and [lem-coef-pointed-model-stability] identifies the ordinary homotopy category of its coherent localization with its ordinary localization. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] the latter is $D(R)$. Thus these are precisely the morphisms asserted in the item, with no boundedness restriction on $P$ or $C$.

source.place: Qh_map_bijective, lines 43-48, applied to the degree-zero consequence of dg-projectivity; Hovey Theorem 1.2.10(ii) provides the corresponding model-category interpretation.

proof.text: All hypotheses of [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability] hold: combinatoriality, closed symmetric monoidality, the cofibrant unit and the pushout-product condition are supplied by [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model]. Apply that localization theorem. The result is presentable, its symmetric monoidal tensor is $q(QC\otimes QD)$ on cofibrant replacements, and this tensor preserves small colimits separately, including the empty colimit. With the conventions of that theorem, $\mathbf D_\infty(R)$ is exactly the homotopy coherent localization of unbounded $R$-module cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms; this identifies the localization and its derived tensor as asserted. It retains the mapping spaces and their coherences, rather than merely the ordinary derived category.

source.place: Example 5.11, associated monoidal infinity-category of unbounded module complexes; general localization theorem cited in the step supplies presentability and separate cocontinuity.

proof.text: A quasi-isomorphism becomes an equivalence by the defining localization property in [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability]. Conversely, if the image of a chain map $f$ is an equivalence, its image in the ordinary homotopy category is an isomorphism. Step 9 identifies that category and functor with the derived localization. The cohomology functors $H^n:D(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] send this isomorphism to an isomorphism and have composite with localization equal to ordinary cohomology. Therefore every $H^n(f)$ is an isomorphism, which is exactly the definition of a quasi-isomorphism. This proves the reverse implication without assuming a separate saturation theorem.

source.place: Theorem 1.2.10(iv), saturation clause; here deduced directly from the cohomology factorization of the cited derived-category definition.

proof_origin.place: Example 5.11 and Theorem 5.8 hypotheses; explicit supplementary arguments from the projective model of Hovey Theorem 2.3.11, the existing localization theorem, Stacks 0117/05RT/00DB, and the pinned Mathlib K-projective Hom theorem. Primary sources read online where absent locally; archives requested in report.md.
